text:
maria: Heads-up — we just saw a p99 latency ~3x baseline for hosted-prod on west-1 starting ~12:17 UTC. Lots of streaming sessions in the spike window. Anyone else seeing this?

kevin: yep seeing it. tailing inference logs shows a pile of streaming chunk ACK backpressure and lots of long prompt lengths in the same window.

sara: adding profiler dump from one affected worker: 
```
2026-03-18T12:18:02Z worker-17 PROFILE
model: redwood-7b-v2
seq_len_distribution: median=64 p95=512 p99=2048
kernel_selected: grouped_gemm_v1 (fallback path for some ops)
kv_cache_hits: 12% (high miss rate for prefix copies)
batching: 24 requests combined (total_tokens=7380)
avg_latency_per_token_ms: 14.7
queue_wait_ms: 120
observed: allocator thrash + repeated KV copy for long prefixes
```

maria: that p99=2048 jump is suspicious — we haven't had so many long prompts simultaneously. any clue where they're coming from?

devon: quick grep of request traces shows a small set of clients with tool-call loops. pattern: user flow triggers tool call that appends previous assistant text into prompt again (increasing prompt by ~1k tokens per call). they stream and retry on timeout, so backpressure + retries amplify.

kevin: this explains both prompt-length spike and sustained streaming pressure. batching heuristic currently only caps requests per-batch, not total tokens. once a few very-long seqs land we create oversized batches that pick a slower kernel variant.

maria: was kernel selection the main latency multiplier? or KV cache behavior?

sara: both. kernel selection heuristic uses sample seq len stats for the worker. with high variance it sometimes picks a grouped kernel that has worse perf at extreme lengths on these GPUs. plus KV cache copy cost increases linearly with prefix length and we saw thrashing because prefix sharing across requests was low (low hit rate).

opsbot: Scaling action: autoscaler increased dedicated-pool-3 by 2 instances at 12:22 UTC to relieve queue.

devon: mitigation plan I pushed in infra branch to do a hotfix: 1) enforce tokens-per-batch cap (max_total_tokens=4096) 2) add per-request long-seq flag to route to single-request priority path (no batching) 3) add transient retry suppression when streaming backpressure observed. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2438

kevin: +1 test on staging looks good: prevents oversized batching and drops end-to-end p99 back to ~1.2x. small perf cost for long single-shot requests but overall latency SLO recovered.

maria: can we also add a short-term guard to kernel selection so it prefers the low-variance kernel when seq_len_p99 > 1024 and batch_total_tokens > 2048?

sara: yes I have a patch that bumps kernel preference thresholds; will open PR after hotfix merged.

devon: also instrumenting a rule in routing: if streaming session shows >3 consecutive backpressure events, mark client for temp rate-limit and notify app-owner (helps stop the tool-loop amplification).

maria: thanks. opsbot — monitor for recurrence and post metrics for p50/p95/p99 and batch token counts next 30m.

opsbot: Monitoring: created alert rule 'runtime.streaming_backpressure_surge' and started a 30m window check. First snapshot will post at 12:30 UTC.

kevin: after hotfix rollout at 12:28 UTC saw p99 drop to ~1.1x and queue depth steady. leaving a canary 10% traffic for 10m then full rollout.

sara: follow-ups: 1) add unit test for batching algorithm with skewed seq length distributions, 2) extend kernel selection sim harness to surface worst-case tails, 3) write a playbook for tool-call loop patterns so support can triage app-level causes.

maria: adding to eng-runtime backlog and tagging eng-sre for postmortem if we see recurrence. great work on the fast fix everyone. :thumbsup:
